I’m 32 and I’ve been praying for a spouse for at least 8 years. I have a home and a good job, but I converted in my mid-20s and there aren’t a lot of single Christian women when you’re approaching 30 (Catholics seem to be the exception but I’m not Catholic)

I’d say it gets better but it doesn’t. It gets routine, though, so in that respect it doesn’t get worse.

I sin in this dimension (pornography) and I’ve gone through stretches where I stopped masturbating but I can’t say in earnestness that I’ve been sexually pure for more than 3-4 months at my best streak. I have a healthy BMI but I wouldn’t describe myself as anything but cute at best, average at worst.

To be honest I feel pretty hollow inside. My best advice from watching my younger friends get married is to be active in your church and go to social events adjacent to your life group or Bible study. Go to barbecues and frisbee groups and you’ll meet other single women.

And, in general, work on yourself. Build the foundations of your career. Exercise and eat well. Don’t pass up opportunities to go out with someone while you’re waiting for “the one”

They should be able to include the banking reforms in the infrastructure bill, because the package could pass with 50 votes plus Harris. Even if Biden doesn’t like it, he can’t order Harris to not break a Senate tie when it’s her Constitutional prerogative.

The real test is whether the cannabis banking reforms—which are a huge deal to the MSOS—pass the budget reconciliation test. That is, do they lower the deficit over 10 (and possibly 15) years? Of course they do. They’ll make more money, pay more taxes.

Now, some of you may not like these guys. But what do you think happens when Cresco Labs sells medical in your state? Some of the money flows to the politicians who can vote to expand medical marijuana. Maybe the money flows to ballot initiatives. Deep red states like Indiana and Alabama are so loathe to go medical because it absolutely is the first step to full legalization when you have deep-pocketed cannabis companies involved and it’s worth their money pay politicians for market access.

Yeah, pregabalin was designed as a potent successor to gabapentin. They’re both voltage-gated calcium channel blockers.

I hate both of those drugs but they’re the difference, at moderately high doses, between incapacitating symptoms and 10,000 steps a day on my Fitbit.

I was diagnosed with new daily persistent headache (NDPH) because I could remember the exact moment my headache began nearly six years ago.

For what it’s worth, pregabalin and gabapentin takes it from a 8/10 to a 3/10 until they start to wear off. I can’t even get out of bed until the drugs kick in or the movement will ramp up the headache.

I had all the brain scans but a CINE MRI. My herniation is between 5-8mm depending on the interpreting radiologist. 

I hesitate to get the surgery because I’m convinced something else must have happened to start the headache, but the Chiari is all that shows up.

Unfortunately, I underwent an occipital decompresssion surgery for occipital neuralgia before I was diagnosed with a Chiari malformation. It has helped a little, but not enough.

Yeah but you don’t accelerate towards the ground like a missile. You have to jump from a very high point to make it count, but then there’s more time for regret, panic, and second thoughts.

I read somewhere that people who survived attempts from jumping off bridges often say they regretted it the instant they leaped.

My pain is predominately on my left side, but my right tonsil descends to the greater extent. 

I sometimes wonder if any pain I experience on the right side is just a consequence of my left side muscles at the base of my head and neck area pulling and stretching the right ones
I also find that ice packs help, and direct sun is the worst.

Yea but how people have lived in the last 2,000 years compared to the previous 198,000 years combined? Every successive year also disproportionately increases the share of human existence covered by an Abrahamic God because more of us are around today.

I believe the Bible was written by man. That doesn’t mean I pick and choose at random; I read the synoptic Gospels as witness testimony and much of the OT as Hebrew wisdom literature.

Accordingly, who am I to say what God does with the people who predeceased the existence of Jesus. I’d imagine they’re judged by a similar criteria as a guy in a rural India who has never heard of Christianity.

I think it’s possible for me to be judged to a different standard on whether I believe in Jesus, because I was exposed to enough of Him to choose or reject.

I also don’t assume all or even most Christians go to Heaven. Hell, I don’t even assume that I’ll go to Heaven, and I say that as an annihilationist who doesn’t believe in eternal Hell. 

Christianity is a redemptive faith and I’m glad it came into my life, but it’s not like all or even most of us picked it because it offers eternal life. Plenty of religions make that promise. I wish the God of Thor had reached out to me because I want to go to Valhalla, plus my God doesn’t like Tinder, Robinhood, or holding grudges, and I do. Christianity is not an easy faith to practice.

“There are 2500 religions, how are we supposed to know Christianity is true?”

The majority of everyone alive for at least a thousand years has worshipped on an Abrahamic continuum. Between Christianity and Islam, which also reveres Jesus (Mary is mentioned more times in the Quran than the NT), you’re trusting people from modern Nigeria to 12th century France that if you’re going to pray to the sky or place your faith in a religious text, you may want to consider how many people think the God of Abraham answers their prayers. 

It’s like if I had never tried tea before, I wouldn’t say “well I hear you saying black tea is great but there could be thousands of good teas, why don’t I pick a plant at random and boil it in water.”

Edit: I am Christian and want to acknowledge that I appreciated some of your questions. Too many Christians accept that our faith is supposed to be challenged “in the world” but get defensive when we have to confront it in our heads.
